title: A Roman Emperor in the Mekong Mud? The Lost Kingdom of Funan #shorts
description:
A gold pendant copying a Roman emperor's coin turned up at Óc Eo in the Mekong Delta. It wasn't Roman, and it leads to Funan: a kingdom known mostly from Chinese records and from the mud of Óc Eo, with sites in today's Vietnam and Cambodia.

Sources: M. Vickery, 'Funan Reviewed: Deconstructing the Ancients', BEFEO 90–91 (2003); B. Borell, 'The Power of Images: Coin Portraits of Roman Emperors on Jewellery Pendants in Early Southeast Asia', ZAAK 6 (2014); L. Malleret, 'Les fouilles d'Oc-èo (1944)', BEFEO 45 (1951); Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Funan'; UNESCO Tentative Lists: Oc Eo – Ba The (Viet Nam), Angkor Borei and Phnom Da (Cambodia).

Illustrations and narration are AI-assisted. Corrections welcome in the comments.
